column1: # kind|MM-DD|year|Greek name|English name|English biography   (English versions of the short biographies in data/bios; kind is always bio)

bio|08-09|1962|Έρμαν Έσσε|Hermann Hesse|Hermann Hesse died in 1962 in Switzerland. He was a German-Swiss writer and poet. He wrote "Siddhartha", "Steppenwolf" and "The Glass Bead Game", and in 1946 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|08-09|1963|Γουίτνεϊ Χιούστον|Whitney Houston|Whitney Houston was an American singer and actress with a powerful voice. She became known with hits such as "I Will Always Love You" from the film "The Bodyguard". She died in 2012.

bio|08-09|1975|Ντμίτρι Σοστακόβιτς|Dmitri Shostakovich|Dmitri Shostakovich was a Russian composer. He wrote 15 symphonies and 15 string quartets, and his music was linked with the difficult years of the Soviet era, when he was often in disfavour. He died in 1975.
bio|08-10|353|Μαγνέντιος|Magnentius|Magnentius was a Roman usurper. In 350 he overthrew the emperor Constans in the West and was defeated by Constantius II. He committed suicide in 353 in France.

bio|08-10|1759|Φερδινάνδος ΣΤ΄|Ferdinand VI|Ferdinand VI was King of Spain from 1746 to 1759. He followed a policy of neutrality and developed the economy and the navy. After the death of his wife he fell into deep melancholy and died in 1759.

bio|08-10|1810|Καμίλο Μπένσο|Camillo Benso, Count of Cavour|Camillo Benso, Count of Cavour, was an Italian politician from Piedmont. As prime minister of the Kingdom of Sardinia he played a decisive role in the unification of Italy. He died in 1861, a few months after the proclamation of the kingdom.

bio|08-10|1874|Χέρμπερτ Χούβερ|Herbert Hoover|Herbert Hoover was the 31st president of the United States, from 1929 to 1933. His presidency coincided with the stock market crash of 1929 and the Great Depression. Before that he was an engineer and led food aid programmes. He died in 1964.

bio|08-10|1896|Ότο Λίλιενταλ|Otto Lilienthal|Otto Lilienthal was a German engineer and a pioneer of aviation. He made thousands of glider flights, and his photographs influenced the Wright brothers. He was killed in 1896 in a fall.

bio|08-10|1912|Χόρχε Αμάντο|Jorge Amado|Jorge Amado was a Brazilian writer. He wrote novels about the everyday life of Bahia, such as "Dona Flor and Her Two Husbands" and "Gabriela, Clove and Cinnamon". He died in 2001.

bio|08-10|1951|Χουάν Μανουέλ Σάντος|Juan Manuel Santos|Juan Manuel Santos is a Colombian politician. He was president of Colombia from 2010 to 2018, and in 2016 he was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for the peace agreement with the FARC rebels.

bio|08-10|1960|Αντόνιο Μπαντέρας|Antonio Banderas|Antonio Banderas is a Spanish actor from Málaga. He first worked with Almodóvar and then built a career in Hollywood, with films such as "The Mask of Zorro" and "Puss in Boots".

bio|08-10|1960|Φρανκ Λόιντ|Frank Lloyd|Frank Lloyd was a Scottish director who lived in Hollywood. He won the Best Director Oscar twice and directed the film "Mutiny on the Bounty" in 1935. He died in 1960.

bio|08-11|1253|Κλάρα της Ασίζης|Clare of Assisi|Clare of Assisi was an Italian saint. She followed Francis of Assisi and founded the order of the Poor Ladies, known as the Poor Clares. She died in 1253 and was canonised by the Roman Catholic Church.

bio|08-11|1464|Νικόλαος Κουζάνος|Nicholas of Cusa|Nicholas of Cusa was a German cardinal, philosopher and mathematician. In his work "On Learned Ignorance" he argued that human knowledge of the infinite is limited. He also worked on the union of the Churches. He died in 1464.

bio|08-11|1897|Ένιντ Μπλάιτον|Enid Blyton|Enid Blyton was an English writer of children's books. She wrote more than 700 books, with series such as "The Famous Five" and "The Secret Seven". She remains one of the most widely read authors. She died in 1968.

bio|08-11|1943|Περβέζ Μουσάραφ|Pervez Musharraf|Pervez Musharraf was a Pakistani general and politician. He came to power in a coup in 1999 and was president of Pakistan until 2008. He died in 2023 in Dubai.
bio|08-11|1950|Στιβ Βόζνιακ|Steve Wozniak|Steve Wozniak is an American engineer. He co-founded Apple in 1976 with Steve Jobs and designed the Apple I and Apple II computers.

bio|08-11|1953|Χαλκ Χόγκαν|Hulk Hogan|Hulk Hogan, whose real name was Terry Bollea, was an American professional wrestler and actor. He became one of the biggest names in WWE in the 1980s. He died in 2025.

bio|08-11|1956|Τζάκσον Πόλοκ|Jackson Pollock|Jackson Pollock was an American painter and a leading figure of abstract expressionism. He became known for the "drip painting" method, in which paint dripped onto the canvas. He was killed in a car accident in 1956.
bio|08-11|1983|Κρις Χέμσγουορθ|Chris Hemsworth|Chris Hemsworth is an Australian actor. He became known as Thor in the Marvel films and played in the films "Rush" and "Extraction".

bio|08-11|2014|Ρόμπιν Ουίλιαμς|Robin Williams|Robin Williams died in 2014. He was an American actor and comedian, known for his improvisation. He won an Oscar for his performance in "Good Will Hunting".

bio|08-12|1827|Ουίλλιαμ Μπλέηκ|William Blake|William Blake was an English poet, painter and engraver. He wrote and illustrated "Songs of Innocence and of Experience", in a mystical style. He was not widely known while he was alive. He died in 1827.

bio|08-12|1866|Χαθίντο Μπεναβέντε|Jacinto Benavente|Jacinto Benavente was born in 1866 in Madrid. He was a Spanish playwright with more than a hundred works. In 1922 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1954.

bio|08-12|1881|Σεσίλ Μπ. ντε Μιλ|Cecil B. DeMille|Cecil B. DeMille was an American director and producer. He made large epic films, such as "The Ten Commandments" and "The Greatest Show on Earth", which won an Oscar. He died in 1959.

bio|08-12|1887|Έρβιν Σρέντινγκερ|Erwin Schrödinger|Erwin Schrödinger was an Austrian physicist and one of the founders of quantum mechanics. He formulated the Schrödinger equation and devised the thought experiment with the cat. In 1933 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics. He died in 1961.

bio|08-12|1930|Τζωρτζ Σόρος|George Soros|George Soros was born in Budapest and is an American investor and philanthropist. He became known for his clash with the Bank of England in 1992 and founded the Open Society Foundations.

bio|08-12|1954|Φρανσουά Ολλάντ|François Hollande|François Hollande is a French politician. He was president of France from 2012 to 2017, as the Socialist candidate, and during his term the 2015 attacks in Paris took place.

bio|08-12|1955|Τόμας Μαν|Thomas Mann|Thomas Mann was a German writer. He wrote "Buddenbrooks", "Death in Venice" and "The Magic Mountain". In 1929 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature, and he left Germany under Hitler. He died in 1955.

bio|08-12|1964|Ίαν Φλέμινγκ|Ian Fleming|Ian Fleming was an English writer and journalist, and an intelligence officer in the war. He created the secret agent James Bond in the books that began in 1953. He died in 1964.
bio|08-12|2014|Λορίν Μπακόλ|Lauren Bacall|Lauren Bacall was an American actress. She became known with the film "To Have and Have Not" and was married to Humphrey Bogart. She died in 2014.

bio|08-13|1863|Ευγένιος Ντελακρουά|Eugène Delacroix|Eugène Delacroix was a French painter and a leading figure of Romanticism. He painted "Liberty Leading the People" and "The Massacre at Chios", with the Greek War of Independence as its theme. He died in 1863.

bio|08-13|1871|Καρλ Λίμπκνεχτ|Karl Liebknecht|Karl Liebknecht was a German socialist. Together with Rosa Luxemburg he founded the Spartacus League and later the Communist Party of Germany. He was murdered in 1919.
bio|08-13|1899|Άλφρεντ Χίτσκοκ|Alfred Hitchcock|Alfred Hitchcock was a British director, the "master of suspense". He directed "Psycho", "The Birds", "Vertigo" and "Rear Window". He died in 1980.

bio|08-13|1910|Φλόρενς Νάιτινγκεϊλ|Florence Nightingale|Florence Nightingale was a British nurse and statistician. During the Crimean War she improved the conditions of care for the wounded, and she is considered the founder of modern nursing. She died in 1910.

bio|08-13|1918|Φρέντερικ Σάνγκερ|Frederick Sanger|Frederick Sanger was an English biochemist. He won two Nobel Prizes in Chemistry, in 1958 for the structure of insulin and in 1980 for the method of determining the sequence of DNA. He died in 2013.

bio|08-13|1926|Φιντέλ Κάστρο|Fidel Castro|Fidel Castro was a Cuban revolutionary and politician. He overthrew Batista in 1959 and governed Cuba as a communist leader for decades. He handed power to his brother Raúl and died in 2016.

bio|08-13|1946|Χ. Τζ. Γουέλς|H. G. Wells|H. G. Wells was an English writer and a pioneer of science fiction. He wrote "The Time Machine", "The War of the Worlds" and "The Invisible Man". He died in 1946.

bio|08-13|1970|Άλαν Σίρερ|Alan Shearer|Alan Shearer is a former English footballer who played as a forward. He played for Southampton, Blackburn and Newcastle and is the top scorer in the history of the Premier League.

bio|08-13|1984|Τιγκράν Πετροσιάν|Tigran Petrosian|Tigran Petrosian was an Armenian chess player of the Soviet Union. He was world champion from 1963 to 1969 and was known for his defensive technique. He died in 1984.

bio|08-14|1777|Χανς Κρίστιαν Έρστεντ|Hans Christian Ørsted|Hans Christian Ørsted was a Danish physicist. In 1820 he discovered that an electric current creates a magnetic field, linking electricity with magnetism. He died in 1851.

bio|08-14|1867|Τζον Γκόλσγουορθι|John Galsworthy|John Galsworthy was an English writer. He wrote the novel series "The Forsyte Saga" and plays. In 1932 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1933.

bio|08-14|1956|Μπέρτολτ Μπρεχτ|Bertolt Brecht|Bertolt Brecht was a German playwright and poet. He wrote "The Threepenny Opera", "Mother Courage and Her Children" and "Galileo", and he developed epic theatre. He died in 1956.

bio|08-14|1959|Μάτζικ Τζόνσον|Magic Johnson|Magic Johnson is a former American basketball player. He played for the Los Angeles Lakers, with whom he won five NBA championships. In 1991 he announced that he was HIV-positive.

bio|08-14|1966|Χάλι Μπέρι|Halle Berry|Halle Berry is an American actress. In 2002 she became the first African American to win the Oscar for Best Actress, for "Monster's Ball". She also played Storm in "X-Men".

bio|08-14|1983|Μίλα Κούνις|Mila Kunis|Mila Kunis was born in Ukraine and grew up in the United States. She is an actress. She became known through the series "That '70s Show" and appeared in the films "Black Swan" and "Ted".

bio|08-14|1988|Έντσο Φερράρι|Enzo Ferrari|Enzo Ferrari was an Italian racing driver and the founder of Ferrari. He started as a driver and then founded the racing team Scuderia Ferrari. He died in 1988.
bio|08-14|1994|Ελίας Κανέττι|Elias Canetti|Elias Canetti died in 1994 in Zurich. He was a writer born in Bulgaria who wrote in German, and in 1981 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|08-14|2004|Τσέσλαφ Μίλος|Czesław Miłosz|Czesław Miłosz died in 2004 in Kraków. He was a Polish poet and essayist who lived for many years in the United States, and in 1980 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|08-15|423|Φλάβιος Ονώριος|Honorius|Honorius was a Roman emperor of the West from 395 to 423, the son of Theodosius I. During his reign the Visigoths of Alaric sacked Rome in 410. The capital was moved to Ravenna.

bio|08-15|1038|Στέφανος Α΄|Stephen I|Stephen I was the first king of Hungary. He converted the country to Christianity and was crowned in the year 1000 or 1001. The Catholic Church honours him as a saint, and his death took place in 1038.

bio|08-15|1769|Ναπολέων Βοναπάρτης|Napoleon Bonaparte|Napoleon Bonaparte was born in 1769 in Corsica. He became a general of the French Revolution and Emperor of the French in 1804. He was exiled to Saint Helena after the Battle of Waterloo and died in 1821.
bio|08-15|1771|Γουόλτερ Σκοτ|Walter Scott|Walter Scott was a Scottish writer. He is considered the creator of the historical novel, with works such as "Ivanhoe". He died in 1832.

bio|08-15|1892|Λουί ντε Μπρολί|Louis de Broglie|Louis de Broglie was a French physicist. He proposed that particles also have a wave nature, and in 1929 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics. He died in 1987.

bio|08-15|1936|Γκράτσια Ντελέντα|Grazia Deledda|Grazia Deledda was an Italian writer from Sardinia. She wrote novels about life on the island, and in 1926 she was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. She died in 1936.

bio|08-15|1967|Ρενέ Μαγκρίτ|René Magritte|René Magritte was a Belgian surrealist painter. He painted everyday objects in paradoxical settings, as in "The Treachery of Images", which shows a pipe with the words "This is not a pipe". He died in 1967.

bio|08-15|1972|Μπεν Άφλεκ|Ben Affleck|Ben Affleck is an American actor, screenwriter and director. He won the Oscar for Best Original Screenplay for "Good Will Hunting", together with Matt Damon, and he directed "Argo".

bio|08-15|1990|Τζένιφερ Λόρενς|Jennifer Lawrence|Jennifer Lawrence is an American actress. She became known as Katniss in "The Hunger Games" and won the Oscar for Best Actress for "Silver Linings Playbook".

bio|08-16|1888|Τ. Ε. Λόρενς|T. E. Lawrence|T. E. Lawrence was a British officer. In the First World War he took part in the Arab Revolt against the Ottomans and became known as "Lawrence of Arabia". He wrote the book "Seven Pillars of Wisdom". He died in 1935.

bio|08-16|1913|Μεναχέμ Μπέγκιν|Menachem Begin|Menachem Begin was born in present-day Belarus. He was an Israeli politician and prime minister of Israel from 1977 to 1983. In 1978 he shared the Nobel Peace Prize with Sadat for the Camp David Accords.

bio|08-16|1920|Τσαρλς Μπουκόφσκι|Charles Bukowski|Charles Bukowski was born in Germany and lived in Los Angeles. He was a writer and poet, known for his realistic and raw description of the lives of outsiders. He died in 1994.

bio|08-16|1949|Μάργκαρετ Μίτσελ|Margaret Mitchell|Margaret Mitchell was an American writer. She wrote the novel "Gone with the Wind", which won the Pulitzer Prize and became a famous film. She died in 1949 after a road accident.
bio|08-16|1954|Τζέιμς Κάμερον|James Cameron|James Cameron is a Canadian director. He directed "The Terminator", "Titanic" and "Avatar", which broke box-office records. "Titanic" won 11 Oscars.
bio|08-16|1958|Μαντόνα|Madonna|Madonna is an American singer, songwriter and actress. She is considered one of the most important pop artists, with hits such as "Like a Virgin" and "Vogue".

bio|08-16|1977|Έλβις Πρίσλεϊ|Elvis Presley|Elvis Presley was an American singer and actor, known as "the King of Rock and Roll". He became famous in the 1950s with hits such as "Heartbreak Hotel". He died in 1977 in Memphis, at the age of 42.

bio|08-16|2003|Ιντί Αμίν|Idi Amin|Idi Amin was dictator of Uganda from 1971 to 1979. During his time tens of thousands of people were killed, and he expelled the Asians of the country. He was overthrown and died in exile in Saudi Arabia.
bio|08-16|2018|Αρέθα Φράνκλιν|Aretha Franklin|Aretha Franklin was an American soul singer, known as "the Queen of Soul". She recorded hits such as "Respect" and "Think". She died in 2018.

bio|08-17|1601|Πιερ ντε Φερμά|Pierre de Fermat|Pierre de Fermat was a French lawyer and mathematician. He contributed to number theory and formulated "Fermat's Last Theorem", which was proved only in 1994 by Andrew Wiles. He died in 1665.

bio|08-17|1786|Ντέιβι Κρόκετ|Davy Crockett|Davy Crockett was an American fighter, explorer and politician from Tennessee. He became a member of Congress and was killed in 1836 at the Battle of the Alamo, during the Texas War of Independence.

bio|08-17|1786|Φρειδερίκος Β΄|Frederick II|Frederick II, known as Frederick the Great, was King of Prussia from 1740. He expanded the state through military victories and reforms, and he was also a flautist and composer. He is considered a representative of enlightened despotism.

bio|08-17|1850|Χοσέ ντε Σαν Μαρτίν|José de San Martín|José de San Martín was an Argentine general. He led the struggle for the independence of Argentina, Chile and Peru from Spain and is regarded as a national hero. He died in France in 1850.

bio|08-17|1932|Βιντιαντάρ Σουρατζπρασάντ Νάιπολ|V. S. Naipaul|V. S. Naipaul was born in Trinidad, into a family of Indians, and lived in England. He was a writer. He wrote "A House for Mr Biswas" and in 2001 was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 2018.
bio|08-17|1943|Ρόμπερτ Ντε Νίρο|Robert De Niro|Robert De Niro is an American actor. He often worked with Martin Scorsese in "Taxi Driver", "Raging Bull" and "Goodfellas". He has won two Oscars.

bio|08-17|1953|Χέρτα Μύλερ|Herta Müller|Herta Müller was born in Romania and is a German writer. In her works she describes life under Ceaușescu's regime. In 2009 she was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|08-17|1969|Όττο Στερν|Otto Stern|Otto Stern was a German physicist. He studied the properties of molecules with molecular beams and measured the magnetic moment of the proton. In 1943 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics. He died in 1969.

bio|08-17|1969|Λούντβιχ Μις φαν ντερ Ρόε|Ludwig Mies van der Rohe|Ludwig Mies van der Rohe was a German architect. He directed the Bauhaus and then emigrated to the United States. He became known for his minimalist architecture of glass and steel and for the phrase "less is more".

bio|08-18|1227|Τζένγκις Χαν|Genghis Khan|Genghis Khan was the founder of the Mongol Empire. He united the Mongol tribes in 1206 and conquered a large part of Asia. He died in 1227 on campaign, and the empire was expanded further by his successors.

bio|08-18|1830|Φραγκίσκος Ιωσήφ Α΄|Franz Joseph I|Franz Joseph I was Emperor of Austria and King of Hungary from 1848 to 1916, one of the longest reigns in Europe. The murder of his heir in 1914 led to the First World War.
bio|08-18|1850|Ονορέ ντε Μπαλζάκ|Honoré de Balzac|Honoré de Balzac was a French writer. He wrote the cycle of novels "The Human Comedy", with about 90 works depicting French society. He died in 1850.

bio|08-18|1933|Ρομάν Πολάνσκι|Roman Polanski|Roman Polanski was born in Paris and grew up in Poland. He directed the films "Rosemary's Baby", "Chinatown" and "The Pianist", for which he won the Oscar for Best Director.

bio|08-18|1936|Ρόμπερτ Ρέντφορντ|Robert Redford|Robert Redford was an American actor and director. He acted in the films "Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid" and "The Sting", and he founded the Sundance independent film festival. He died in 2025.
bio|08-18|1952|Πάτρικ Σουέιζι|Patrick Swayze|Patrick Swayze was an American actor and dancer. He became known with the films "Dirty Dancing" and "Ghost". He died in 2009.
bio|08-18|1969|Έντουαρντ Νόρτον|Edward Norton|Edward Norton is an American actor. He became known with the films "American History X" and "Fight Club". He has been nominated for an Oscar.

bio|08-18|1990|Μπ. Φ. Σκίνερ|B. F. Skinner|B. F. Skinner was an American psychologist. He is considered one of the pioneers of behaviourism and developed the concept of operant conditioning. He died in 1990.

bio|08-18|2009|Κιμ Ντε-τζουνγκ|Kim Dae-jung|Kim Dae-jung was a South Korean politician. He was president of South Korea from 1998 to 2003, and in 2000 he was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for his policy of engagement with North Korea. He died in 2009.

bio|08-19|14|Οκταβιανός Αύγουστος|Augustus|Augustus was the first Roman emperor. The adopted son of Julius Caesar, he defeated Antony at Actium in 31 BC and ruled until his death in AD 14, having established the Pax Romana.

bio|08-19|1662|Μπλεζ Πασκάλ|Blaise Pascal|Blaise Pascal was a French mathematician, physicist and philosopher. He built one of the first calculating machines and wrote the "Pensées", with religious and philosophical content. He died in 1662, at the age of 39.

bio|08-19|1871|Όρβιλ Ράιτ|Orville Wright|Orville Wright was an American aviation pioneer. Together with his brother Wilbur he flew the first powered aeroplane on 17 December 1903, at Kitty Hawk. He died in 1948.

bio|08-19|1883|Κοκό Σανέλ|Coco Chanel|Coco Chanel was a French fashion designer and the founder of the Chanel house. She brought simple lines and the little black dress into fashion and created the Chanel No. 5 perfume. She died in 1971.

bio|08-19|1936|Φεδερίκο Γκαρθία Λόρκα|Federico García Lorca|Federico García Lorca was a Spanish poet and playwright. He wrote "Poet in New York" and "Blood Wedding". He was executed in 1936 in Andalusia, at the start of the Spanish Civil War.

bio|08-19|1946|Μπιλ Κλίντον|Bill Clinton|Bill Clinton is the 42nd president of the United States, from 1993 to 2001. Before that he was governor of Arkansas. During his term the economy grew, and there was an impeachment process, from which he was acquitted.

bio|08-19|1951|Ζαν-Λυκ Μελανσόν|Jean-Luc Mélenchon|Jean-Luc Mélenchon is a French left-wing politician. He founded the party "La France Insoumise" and was a candidate in the presidential elections of 2012, 2017 and 2022.
bio|08-19|1969|Μάθιου Πέρι|Matthew Perry|Matthew Perry was an American-Canadian actor. He became famous as Chandler Bing in the series "Friends". He died in 2023.

bio|08-19|1994|Λάινους Πόλινγκ|Linus Pauling|Linus Pauling was an American chemist. He was awarded two Nobel Prizes, in Chemistry in 1954 and in Peace in 1962, for his action against nuclear tests. He studied the nature of the chemical bond.

bio|08-20|1833|Μπέντζαμιν Χάρισον|Benjamin Harrison|Benjamin Harrison was the 23rd president of the United States, from 1889 to 1893. He was the grandson of President William Henry Harrison. He died in 1901.

bio|08-20|1890|Χάουαρντ Φίλιπς Λάβκραφτ|H. P. Lovecraft|Howard Phillips Lovecraft was an American writer. He wrote horror and science fiction stories, such as "The Call of Cthulhu". He became known after his death, in 1937.

bio|08-20|1915|Πάουλ Έρλιχ|Paul Ehrlich|Paul Ehrlich was a German physician and scientist. A pioneer of immunology and chemotherapy, he discovered salvarsan, a drug for syphilis. In 1908 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.
bio|08-20|1917|Αδόλφος φον Μπάιερ|Adolf von Baeyer|Adolf von Baeyer was a German chemist. He synthesised indigo and in 1905 was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry. He died in 1917.

bio|08-20|1944|Ρατζίβ Γκάντι|Rajiv Gandhi|Rajiv Gandhi was an Indian politician. He was prime minister of India from 1984 to 1989, after the assassination of his mother Indira Gandhi. He was assassinated in 1991.

bio|08-20|1961|Πέρσι Γουίλλιαμς Μπρίντγκμαν|Percy Williams Bridgman|Percy Williams Bridgman was an American physicist. He studied the behaviour of matter at very high pressures and in 1946 was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics. He took his own life in 1961 while he was ill.
bio|08-20|1983|Άντριου Γκάρφιλντ|Andrew Garfield|Andrew Garfield is a British-American actor. He played in "The Social Network" and in "The Amazing Spider-Man", as Spider-Man.
bio|08-20|1992|Ντέμι Λοβάτο|Demi Lovato|Demi Lovato is an American singer and actress. She started on Disney television and became known with hits such as "Heart Attack" and "Sorry Not Sorry".

bio|08-20|2017|Τζέρι Λιούις|Jerry Lewis|Jerry Lewis was an American comedian and actor. He became known for his comedy duo with Dean Martin and for films such as "The Nutty Professor". He died in 2017.

bio|08-21|1765|Γουλιέλμος Δ΄|William IV|William IV was King of the United Kingdom from 1830 to 1837, when the Reform Act of 1832 was passed. He was the third son of George III. As a young man he served in the Royal Navy.

bio|08-21|1940|Λέων Τρότσκι|Leon Trotsky|Leon Trotsky was a Russian revolutionary. He led the Red Army and was a main rival of Stalin. He was exiled and murdered in 1940 in Mexico by an agent of Stalin.

bio|08-21|1963|Μοχάμετ ΣΤ'|Mohammed VI|Mohammed VI has been King of Morocco since 1999. He succeeded his father, Hassan II. During his reign reforms have taken place, such as the revision of family law.
bio|08-21|1973|Σεργκέι Μπριν|Sergey Brin|Sergey Brin was born in Moscow and grew up in the United States. He co-founded Google with Larry Page in 1998, while they were students at Stanford.

bio|08-21|1979|Τζιουζέπε Μεάτσα|Giuseppe Meazza|Giuseppe Meazza was an Italian footballer. He played for Inter and Milan and won two World Cups with Italy, in 1934 and 1938. The San Siro stadium bears his name. He died in 1979.

bio|08-21|1986|Γιουσέιν Μπολτ|Usain Bolt|Usain Bolt is a former Jamaican sprinter. He holds the world records in the 100 metres, with 9.58 seconds, and in the 200 metres, and he won eight Olympic gold medals.

bio|08-21|1988|Ρόμπερτ Λεβαντόφσκι|Robert Lewandowski|Robert Lewandowski is a Polish footballer who plays as a forward. He played for Bayern Munich, where he scored many goals, and later for Barcelona. He is the top scorer of the Polish national team.

bio|08-21|1995|Σουμπραμανιάν Τσαντρασεκάρ|Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar|Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar was an Indian-American astrophysicist. He calculated the Chandrasekhar limit, the maximum mass of a white dwarf, and in 1983 he shared the Nobel Prize in Physics. He died in 1995.
